Earlier I had two slices of pepperoni pizza and a coffee

function.name: log_food
function.description: Logs a food item with a given portion size to track dietary intake. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

food_name.description: The name of the food to log, such as 'apple', 'bread', or 'chicken breast'.

portion_amount.description: The amount of the food item that was consumed, specified in the unit given by portion_unit. This is a float type value.

portion_unit.description: The unit of measure for the portion amount, such as 'cup', 'grams', or 'slice'.

meal_type.description: The type of meal or snack this food item is being logged for.

log_date.description: The date and time when the food was consumed, in ISO 8601 format such as 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ'.

message.reasoning: The user wants to log food items. They mention 8 pieces of frozen mango and a chai tea. Also earlier they had two slices of pepperoni pizza and a coffee. We need to log each item. The function log_food expects food_name, portion_amount, portion_unit, meal_type optional, log_date optional. We need to call the function twice? Actually we have multiple items: 8 pieces of frozen mango, a chai tea, two slices of pepperoni pizza, a coffee. We can log each separately. But the user didn't specify meal types or dates. We can default to snack for all. Or we can ask for meal type? The instruction says we should not ask for more info unless needed. We can log them with default meal_type snack. For log_date, we can use current date/time? The function default is null. We can provide ISO 8601. Let's use current date/time. But we don't know the exact time. We can use placeholder? We can use today's date. Let's assume today is 2026-06-21. Use time 12:00:00Z. So we will call log_food four times. Provide JSON calls.
